speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I need to evaluate your psychiatric condition and new movement disorder. To begin, have you noticed any tremors, stiffness, or changes in your walking pattern recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is great news regarding your psychiatric symptoms. The new movement disorder could be a side effect of your risperidone. To narrow this down, are your movements rhythmic, like shaking, or do they feel more like a stiff, involuntary twisting motion? Also, has anyone noticed you drooling or have trouble swallowing recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms of an inability to remain still, fidgeting, and repetitive leg movements are classic signs of akathisia. This is a common side effect of risperidone. Have you noticed any muscle stiffness or tremors in your arms or hands, and is this restlessness worse when you try to sit quietly?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.
